subject: Data handling & subprocessors — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data handling & subprocessors — follow-up and next steps

Hi Ellen — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of Acme requirements we heard today:
- PII scoping: customer will send user-generated content (names, emails, occasional customer support transcripts).
- Data residency: all production inference and logs must remain in US regions (no EU/APAC replication).
- Retention: preference for 90-day retention for logs and artifacts; happy to discuss shorter windows for certain telemetry.
- Logging & audit: Acme needs exportable audit logs for admin actions and a rolling export for incident investigations.
- Third-party sharing: any telemetry/analytics vendor access must be disclosed and contractually restricted; no transfer of user PII without DPA amendment.

Immediate asks from Acme we can action: 
1) Provide a current list of Redwood subprocessors and high-level descriptions of what they process (telemetry, hosting, payments, monitoring).
2) Confirm which telemetry vendors receive aggregated usage data vs. any vendor that might ever receive user-level content.
3) Share SOC 2 report and our standard DPA (attached).
4) Schedule a follow-up call with our Security/SE to walk through retention, logging exports, and optional on-prem/private deployment options.

Next steps (proposed):
- I'll attach the subprocessors list and the DPA and SOC2.
- Can we get time for a 45-min technical follow-up this week? Rishi (SE) & Dev (InfoSec) are on copy.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_2026.csv; SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf; data_processing_addendum_2026.pdf

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Hi Marissa — appreciate the recap and attachments. A few clarifying Qs from our security/compliance team after a quick review:

1) Telemetry vendors: can you explicitly call out any vendor that receives telemetry tied to a customer identifier? We need to know if any vendor could map usage to Acme users.
2) Marketplace flows: our procurement team is concerned about any marketplace integrations (e.g., cloud marketplace billing flows) that might surface usage or billing metadata to third parties — can you confirm what flows exist and whether billing/usage is visible to marketplace partners?
3) Cloud provider / region: you noted US-only — can you confirm which cloud regions (AWS/GCP) and whether any backups or disaster recovery runs out-of-region?

I'm attaching a short compliance checklist the team uses — it'll help us mark must-haves vs. nice-to-haves.

We can do a technical follow-up tomorrow afternoon. Please include Rishi and Dev.

Thanks,

Thanks Ellen — looping in Rishi and Dev to confirm the technical details; Laura from legal is copied for the DPA/contract questions. Quick answers to your bullets below, with more detail from Rishi/Dev on the follow-up call: 

- Telemetry vendors: Redwood sends aggregated, non-PII telemetry to an external analytics vendor (Telemetry-Viz) for product usage dashboards. We do not send user content or PII to that vendor by default. We can provide a configuration toggle for Acme to disable telemetry forwarding for your org. See attached subprocessors list (redwood_subprocessors_2026.csv) — Telemetry-Viz is listed as "usage analytics (aggregated)".
- Marketplace flows: our hosted API offering supports cloud marketplace billing (AWS/Azure) but billing metadata is limited — marketplace partners do not receive user content. We can provide a marketplace-specific dataflow diagram on the call.
- Cloud regions / backups: production inference runs in AWS us-east-1 by default for Acme; backups and cross-region DR snapshots are not enabled for us unless configured. We can restrict all processing and backups to us-east-1 for Acme under a Dedicated or Private deployment.

Attachments included: redwood_subprocessors_2026.csv; data_processing_addendum_2026.pdf; SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf

Proposed next step: Technical deep-dive tomorrow 16 Mar, 3:00pm PT with Rishi and Dev to walk through logs, retention windows, and telemetry config. Does that work for you?

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data handling & subprocessors — follow-up and next steps

Hi Ellen — quick technical notes ahead of the call: 

- Audit logs & retention: by default our hosted logs (admin actions, API request metadata) are retained for 30 days. For customers with retention requirements we support configuration to 90 days (or customer-specified windows) and can provide export hooks (S3 export or secure streaming) for your SIEM/forensics.
- Data in-flight & at-rest: inference input/outputs are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest using KMS-managed keys. We offer customer-managed CMKs for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- KV cache / transient state: KV caches used for session performance are kept in volatile memory and are not persisted to long-term storage; they are not part of audit logs or backups.
- Telemetry vendor (Telemetry-Viz): receives aggregated, aggregated-only metrics by default (no user identifiers). We have an internal process to do a PIA for each vendor; the subprocessors CSV maps vendor -> data category -> legal basis. If needed, we can provide a redacted vendor contract and a technical dataflow diagram.
- Marketplace billing metadata: marketplace partners may see aggregated usage metrics for billing but do not receive request payloads or user content.

Links/resources for the call: SOC2 report and DPA already attached by Marissa. Additional resources: https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/security-resources-RW

Happy to go deeper on any of these during the call — see you at 3:00pm PT.

-Rishi
Security & Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
